key_insight: LLM agents can act as practical natural-language schedulers for home energy management, matching MILP-like performance when connected to live pricing, weather, solar, and appliance data through native tool calling.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a deployable interface for optimizing household loads that could improve demand response participation, reduce electricity bills, and simplify constraint-based scheduling for users.
method: Tool-calling ReAct agent for multi-appliance scheduling
Uses live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, PV estimates, usage data, and RAG knowledge base
Benchmarked against MILP ground truth across tariff, conflict, solar, and week-long scenarios
evidence_signal: Across three commercial models, native function calling achieved 100% scheduling success with 96.7-98.0% of oracle savings over a simulated week and projected about GBP 1,270 annual savings versus an off-peak timer baseline.
watch_item: Reliability drops sharply when actions are text-parsed instead of natively called, so robust tool integration and safety checks are essential before real-world deployment.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
